newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber said quiet, spot deals done.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber said quiet, spot deals done.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was largely quiet at the close on Monday although some consumers were said to have done some spot deals for SIR20 rubber from Indonesia, dealers said.
"I heard there was some buying for SIR20 rubber from Indonesia," a dealer said.
But the rest of the market was quiet, with the Songkran Buddhist New Year holiday in Thailand sidelining most of the Thai sellers in the regional rubber market, dealers said.
"It was quiet. Most of the buyers were sidelined by Songkran," one trader said.
One market analyst said dealers may be trying to talk down prices by constantly harping on weak consumer buying. "I think they're trying to talk the prices down," the analyst said.
Market activity may suffer more when the Eid Al-Adha Moslem holiday on Friday shuts down markets in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, dealers said.

At around 0945 GMT, August RSS3 was seen at 115.00-116.00 U.S. cents a kg from 116.50 cents. July RSS1 was seen at 165.75 Singapore cents (US$1.15) a kg from 167.75 cents. June TSR20 was indicated at 156.00-158.00 Singapore cents (US$1.08-$1.09) a kg from 157.00 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
